newsitem.title: HONG KONG: UBS urges caution on Thai, South Korean bonds.
newsitem.headline: UBS urges caution on Thai, South Korean bonds.

text.p: Investors in South Korean and Thai bonds should be wary, Union Bank of Switzerland said on Thursday, citing currency concerns and problems in the Thai bank sector and more problems for South Korea's conglomerates.
"At current levels, certain bonds look very cheap," said Steve Williams, UBS head of fixed income research and new issues.
"Yet we would highlight the likelihood of continued spread volatility in response to ongoing structural adjustments in either country," he said in a statement.
He said there were "currency concerns" in Thailand, and "the potential for conditions in the country's finance sector to get worse".
"For Korea, the probability that more chaebols (conglomerates) will encounter difficulties is high, and this is likely to put further pressure on the country's banks," Williams said.
But he said prospects for the Korean convertible market were more promising, thanks to a weakening of the won against the yen, helping Korean exporters and sparking a stockmarket rally.
UBS continued to recommend an overweight position in China and Hong Kong bonds, he said.

It also maintained an overweight position on Malaysian credits "given their stability and greater resilience to the negative sentiment which affected Asian and emerging markets worldwide earlier this year", Williams said.
